style: Stale Solbakken's fluid 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3 built on an ego-free culture where every player tracks back defensively. In possession the side plays vertically to exploit Erling Haaland's pace and finishing, with Martin Odegaard orchestrating between the lines.
recent_form: Excellent. Norway qualified with a perfect record of eight wins in eight, scoring a UEFA-leading 37 goals (Haaland alone netting 16). One of Europe's in-form sides entering their first World Cup since 1998.

key_players.name: Erling Haaland
key_players.note: Manchester City forward and nation's all-time top scorer (55 goals); scored 16 in qualifying, the focal point of every attack.

key_players.name: Martin Odegaard
key_players.note: Arsenal midfielder who orchestrates the attack and links midfield to Haaland between the lines.

key_players.name: Alexander Sorloth
key_players.note: Powerful striker providing an alternative aerial and target-man threat up front.

key_players.name: Antonio Nusa
key_players.note: Young, direct winger offering dribbling and pace on the flank.

key_players.name: Oscar Bobb
key_players.note: Technical, creative winger adding width and chance creation.

key_players.name: Sander Berge
key_players.note: Tall, all-action midfielder providing balance and ball progression.

historical_news: Norway returns to the World Cup after a 28-year absence, last appearing in 1998.
Qualified with a perfect eight-win record, scoring a UEFA-best 37 goals.
Erling Haaland scored 16 qualifying goals, roughly double any other European player.
Hailed as a 'golden generation' built around Haaland and captain Martin Odegaard.
Drawn into a demanding Group I with two-time champions France, Senegal and Iraq.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Strong buzz around a golden generation and prolific qualifying form, with the main question being whether the supporting cast can match Haaland and Odegaard's quality on the biggest stage.
